claims.text: The Parthenon is an enduring symbol of ancient Greece and Western civilisation, originally built in the 5th century BC as a temple dedicated to the goddess Athena.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It was constructed in thanksgiving for the Greek victory over the Persian invaders during the Greco-Persian Wars.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The name 'Parthenon' derives from the Greek word 'parthénos' meaning maiden or virgin, which likely referred to the unmarried women's apartments or a specific room in the temple.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Like most Greek temples, the building also served a practical purpose as the city treasury, eventually holding the funds of the powerful Delian League.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Over its long history, the structure has been repurposed multiple times, serving as a Christian church in the 6th century AD and later as a mosque following the Ottoman conquest.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The temple suffered its most devastating blow during the Morean War in 1687, when a Venetian bomb hit the building while the Ottomans were using it as a munitions dump.
claims.subject: self
